title: Qwen3 Technical Report
authors: Qwen Team (An Yang, Anfeng Li, Baosong Yang and 57 more core contributors, plus 118 contributors; the full list is §6)
date: May 2025 (arXiv v1 14 May 2025, the only version; models released 29 April 2025)

code.title: QwenLM/Qwen3
code.note: The official repository: model list, quick start with the enable_thinking switch and the /think and /no_think flags, deployment recipes (about 20 minutes for the README and entry path). Weights are on Hugging Face and ModelScope under Apache 2.0; the training code and data are not released

takeaway: One open Apache 2.0 family (0.6B dense to 235B-A22B MoE) fusing thinking and non-thinking modes with a token-budget dial, trained on 36T tokens plus 4-stage post-training, with on-policy distillation beating RL for small models at 1/10 the GPU hours.
verdict: Believe the recipe and the controls it ships: one checkpoint that obeys /think and /no_think, a budget that trades tokens for accuracy, small models distilled cheaply. Read the leaderboards as Qwen's own single runs without error bars, and the two experiments that carry the report's ideas as one-model, one-run evidence: distillation beat RL in one 8B comparison on math and code, and the budget curves come from one model whose 32K points differ from its own Table 11.

resources.t: Understanding and Implementing Qwen3 From Scratch
resources.n: Builds the dense architecture in plain PyTorch; the fastest way to internalise exactly what a Qwen3 block contains (the toy on this page is the same block at d = 32).
Situates Qwen3 dense and MoE against DeepSeek-V3, Llama, Gemma and later designs; good on the no-shared-expert MoE choice.
Release-week analysis of why the size ladder plus Apache 2.0 made Qwen3 the default open family.
The team's own framing of hybrid thinking, the 119-language jump and the agentic focus; it carries claims the report does not (for example Qwen3-4B rivalling Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct).
The model collection: every checkpoint with its card, config.json and the chat template that implements enable_thinking.
The post that ended hybrid thinking at the top of the line: "we decided to stop using hybrid thinking mode".

kb.t: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
kb.n: The reasoning-RL paradigm Qwen3 adopts (cold start, then RL); its distilled models are the baselines Qwen3's small models beat, and Qwen3 answers its distillation-against-RL question for students.
GRPO, the algorithm of Qwen3's reasoning-RL stage, and the Pass@K analysis that Table 21's pass@64 column echoes.
The rival open MoE flagship: Qwen3-235B-A22B-Base beats DeepSeek-V3-Base on 14 of 15 benchmarks with a third of the parameters, without MLA, shared experts or multi-token prediction.
The MoE lineage behind Qwen3's 128 fine-grained experts with 8 active, and the auxiliary balancing loss that Qwen3 computes over the global batch.
The open MoE that made top-k routing standard; Qwen3 keeps the router and drops Mixtral's few large experts for many small ones.
Rotary embeddings, extended here by raising the base to 1,000,000 (ABF) and by YaRN and Dual Chunk Attention at inference.
The competing open-family report a year earlier; Qwen3's comparisons against Llama-4 Maverick and Scout mark the open-weight lead moving east.

topics.n: The lab page: Qwen's architecture choices, global-batch balancing animated, the thinking-budget strip, the Table 21 bars, the whole lineage after this report (2507 split, Next, 3.5 to 3.8) and the licences.
The comparison across labs, and the Deeper: test-time compute tab on reasoning budgets.
Post-training recipes: SFT, preference optimisation, reasoning RL and distillation.
Reinforcement learning, including RL with verifiable rewards.
Pre-training data pipelines, synthetic data and mixture optimisation.

topics.t: RL for LLMs: RLHF, GRPO, RLVR
topics.n: The RL machinery behind stages 2 and 4, including GSPO, the Qwen team's sequence-level variant of GRPO.
